question: The instructions are what a person asked for. It was done directly, by hand, and all there is to see of it is in this summary. Answer one question: was what the person asked for got? recordSets holds rows really read from the site. acts lists the lasting acts really done on the site, each with its state: landed, it happened; may_have_landed, it ran and its effect is not known; undone, it was taken back; not_done, it never happened. endView is how the site looked at the end. witnesses.before and witnesses.after are one reading of the site, taken before the first lasting act and at the end. An act whose words begin 'Already done earlier' was done by an earlier attempt at these same words: it counts as got where the views agree it still stands, and finding the site as it left it is right, not a missing change; doing it again would be wrong. One whose words begin 'May already be done' counts as got only where the views show it. looked lists what looks at the site found after the first lasting act, each with where it was made and what was found there, whole, from the site itself: it is evidence, as the views are. readPages lists the reads the rows in recordSets came from, oldest first, each with where it read (the view of the site, and place, the position in it) and kept, how many rows it kept: the rows are those of every page listed, not only the page endView shows; a page with kept 0 was read the same way and held no row to keep. Where given, keptRows names by label the rows that read kept, and leftOut the rows that read found on the site and did not keep, each set under the conditions the read was asked with that left it out, with what a condition read on the items it left out where the read said: they are items the site showed, as the views are. Where a leftOut set gives sameLabelKept, each label named there is also the label of a row a read kept: the site showed two items under that label, the kept one met every condition of its read and the one in this set did not, so the label being both kept and left out is not one item both kept and dropped. Judge the change, not the absolute state: a place that held 3 before and 4 after has had 1 added, which is what asking to add 1 asks, and its total of 4 is no defect. What already held before is not credit for anything done here. answerText is the model's own words and proves nothing by itself: where it says something, look for it in the rows, the acts and the views. How it was done is not in question, and anything said elsewhere about parts of a record that are not in this summary does not count here: nothing is wrong because it is not shown. Answer yes only when what was asked for was got; no when this evidence shows it was not, naming in observed what is wrong or missing; unknown when this evidence cannot tell. In diagnosis.defects, list an act that was done wrongly as kind other, naming in row what it was done to.
